page2_img_1.png.title: CodeFlow review UI showing files, diffs, reviewers, and comment threads
page2_img_1.png.description: Screenshot of the CodeFlow desktop review window with labeled regions A–F that map to elements described in the paper. (A) The left file tree lists files in the change (including description.txt); (B) the reviewer pane below shows invited reviewers, their roles and sign-off status (checkmarks for sign-offs); (C) the central pane shows a color-coded diff of the selected file with highlighted inline code regions; (F) a floating comment thread popup displays the discussion between reviewers and the author with actions and a “Closed” state; (E) tabs along the top show five iterations of the change (1–5); and (D) the bottom-right pane provides a summary list of comments / threads and their status by file. The window header also indicates review state (e.g., “Completed / Viewing Iteration 1”), illustrating how CodeFlow presents both raw change content and structured review metadata for analysis.

page3_img_2.png.title: World map of code review counts by country and role (developers vs testers)
page3_img_2.png.description: A Power Q&A map visualization (result of querying review counts for Bing in 2014) plotting one pie chart per country where the area of each pie is proportional to the number of completed code reviews. Each pie is split by role: green slices are reviews by developers and orange slices by testers; a tooltip shown over the U.S. reports "Building Country: US, Role: DEV, Code Review Count: 132,594." Most country pies are dominated by green, indicating developers perform the majority of reviews; Europe and Asia show several medium-sized pies while the U.S. has by far the largest circle, and smaller pies appear over Brazil, Australia, and other regions.

page4_img_1.png.title: Bubble chart of average iterations, resolved threads, and files per review by author role (Bing 2015)
page4_img_1.png.description: Power Q&A bubble plot showing author roles in Bing (2015) with average iterations on the x‑axis (≈0.9–2.0), average ever‑resolved threads on the y‑axis (0–3), and bubble area proportional to average files per review. Dev (labelled DEV) appears as the largest bubble at about 1.7 iterations and ~2.4 resolved threads (indicating the largest average files per review), while INTERN is far right (~1.9 iterations, ~2.5 threads) but a smaller bubble. TEST is high on resolved threads (~2.7) at ~1.75 iterations; MANAGER, PM, ARCH, Unknown and CSS occupy mid ranges (≈1.2–1.6 iterations and ~1.1–2.0 resolved threads). RESEARCH is at the low end (~1.0 iterations and ~0 resolved threads).

page3_img_1.png.title: Excel Power View dashboard: CodeFlow Analytics Project Leaderboard
page3_img_1.png.description: An Excel Power View dashboard summarizing CodeFlow metrics for projects. The left panel shows a stacked bar chart “Top 10 CodeFlow Projects by Volume (last 13 mo)” (x-axis in thousands) with Bing highest (approaching the 150K mark) and other projects (AzureAnvil, office16, WinBlueCR, etc.) below it; the bars are color‑stacked by review status (legend: Aborted, Completed, Expired, Stalled) and a banner warns “Too many ‘Project Short Name’ values. Not displaying all data.” The right side contains small multiple line charts: a “Latency Measures (last 5 wk)” chart where one latency series clearly spikes near ~150 hours in week 201349 while the other latency series remain much lower, a “Quality Measures (last 5 wk)” chart showing average reviewers (~3–4), participants and sign‑offs (~2–3) with relatively flat trends, and a chart of iterations/threads/resolved counts showing low single‑digit averages. Below the bar chart are tabular details (source control servers and counts, building names) and a visible filters pane, illustrating that this template provides both high‑level aggregates and drill‑down data for teams to monitor review volume, status, latency, and basic quality indicators.
